key_insight: SLORR is a simple, stateless, architecture-preserving way to make neural network weights more compressible during training by directly regularizing them toward low rank.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical compression-friendly training add-on that avoids costly SVDs, extra trainable layers, and cached state, making it easier to adopt in real deep-learning pipelines.
method: Regularizes original weight matrices during training rather than changing the model architecture
Provides two variants: a Hoyer-sparsity-based regularizer and a nuclear-norm-based regularizer
Uses GPU-friendly forward/backward approximations with approximation guarantees
evidence_signal: The paper reports results on ImageNet-1K for ResNet-50, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/16, and ResNet-18, plus LLM pretraining at 135M and 560M scale, with less than 8% overhead in vision experiments and less than 1% average overhead in LLM training.
watch_item: Approximation quality and training stability may depend on the specific regularizer variant and implementation details, so the low-overhead gains should be validated for each target model and regime.
paper_title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
